author.name: Data Dave
author.role: Builds secure, scalable data pipelines and manages storage infrastructure. Focuses on high-quality data operations and robust data governance. Collaborates on exploring data and managing data quality to support model development.

challenge.name: The Silent Store Gap
challenge.description: A batch of till scan lines from the northern stores was silently dropped during last night's ingestion, causing the model to forecast zero demand for fresh produce. #reliability_ruth# argues that the ingestion pipeline must be fully automated to guarantee every store's data arrives on time, while #data_dave# is willing to accept a manual verification step to ensure data quality before it reaches the feature store.

output.content: I am prepared to accept a manual verification step in the ingestion workflow. This means the nightly data load will not run fully automated, and I will personally review the batch files from the northern stores before they reach the feature store. I am giving up the speed of a zero-touch pipeline and the ability to scale ingestion without adding headcount. In exchange, I get a hard guarantee that no silent data drops, like the missing till scan lines from last night, will ever poison the fresh produce forecasts again. The model must never see zero demand for a store that actually sold goods.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are giving up the speed and scalability of an automated pipeline in exchange for a hard guarantee against data quality issues, which fits the definition of a trade-off.
